core_job: For someone at home or in a small office whose Wi-Fi is fine in one room and bad in another: walk the place, measure Wi-Fi at each named spot with the existing real HTTPS test to speed.cloudflare.com (a new 10 MB / 4 MB spot-check profile), and get a ranked trail of spots saved on the phone. The ranking is pure arithmetic on stored readings (median download, bar scaled to the best spot, a weakest-spot callout). Readings taken after the phone dropped off Wi-Fi are flagged and left out of the ranking.
signature: Rounds, a before-and-after comparison of the same spots. After a change (moving the router, adding a mesh point), the user starts a labelled new round, walks the same spots, and sees the measured change for each spot in download, upload and ping. Each number shows its evidence: the readings used, MB in seconds, and the Cloudflare location (colo) from the keyless https://speed.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace, which I curled today (HTTP 200, returned colo=LAX). The comparison flags when two rounds ran through different colos, or when a spot has only one reading. Competitors are not verified: WebSearch was blocked in this session.
must: M1 Core job end to end: onboarding (type a place name), then Measure here, then name the spot, then a live spot check (new SpeedTestConfig.spotCheck: 10 MB down / 4 MB up / 6 s cap), then the spot is saved and ranked by median Wi-Fi download with a bar relative to the best spot. Quick test (the existing 25 MB/10 MB profile) stays and saves to History. Remove the static Security tab and replace each of its test assertions with a successor test (named in the spec); delete none.

M2 Rounds: Place/Spot/Round/Reading model with Mbps always derived from bytes/ms. New round with a user label. A Compare screen shows per-spot deltas in Mbps and % only for spots measured in both rounds. A spot detail shows MB-in-s evidence and the Cloudflare colo from /cdn-cgi/trace (keep colo only, never store ip=). A different-colo note. A not-on-Wi-Fi flag that excludes the reading from ranking and Compare. Do not use /meta (returns 403 without spoofed browser headers).

M3 Depth: atomic JSON persistence in Application Support with handling for a corrupt file. Multiple places. History with search plus filter chips (place, round, Wi-Fi only / not on Wi-Fi, spot / full). CSV export and text sharing of a comparison via share_plus. Rename and delete with confirmation. Every empty, offline, failure, cancelled, colo-unknown and storage-error state has its own copy.

M4 Own identity: light-default 'survey map' palette (paper #F3F1E7, ink #22262B, spruce #1D5C63, marker #D9822B, strong #3D7A52, weak #A23B4C) plus a dark set (#101A1C/#182528/#5FB3B3/#F0A35A); none of these hexes appears in any repo today. Bundle the Geologica (UI) and Sometype Mono (all figures) OFL fonts, with download URLs curl-verified as 200. The trail is drawn as a route with spot markers. Home is a large place title, a connection strip, a round selector, the ranked trail and a pinned Measure here button. Cupertino nav bar, icons, segmented control and action sheets on iOS. No emoji. Split main.dart into lib/app, lib/data, lib/domain/trail.dart and lib/features/*. Onboarding says 'Where are you measuring?'. Settings is its own screen with a 'How WiFiTrail measures' page.

M5 Remove this app's tells: a new vector icon (dashed trail with a signal dot) and remove the WiFiTrail row from generate_app_icons.py:79. A new splash: storyboard sha must not equal 3f6a9b27d8..., paper background, and Android launch_background to match. CFBundleDisplayName, CFBundleName and android:label become 'WiFiTrail'. Write a real pubspec description. No old class C or Tailwind hexes and no dark-only theme. Move the header language and privacy buttons to Settings. Never store or export SSID, BSSID, IP or location; place and spot names are typed by the user, which keeps the VPN answer true, and a test asserts it. Privacy choices row always visible in Settings.
